spec: Build an event-registration service. Organisers create events with a title, date and capacity; attendees register for an event until it is full, after which registrations are rejected. Every successful registration is also published to an SQS queue for downstream processing. Events and registrations are stored in DynamoDB.

complexity.rationale: Adds a capacity invariant and asynchronous registration event to two related entities.

congruence_checklist: DynamoDB storage for events and registrations
Capacity limit enforced with rejection when full
GET endpoint listing an event's registrations

plan.summary: A FastAPI service for event registration. Organisers create and list events (title, date, capacity); attendees register for an event while seats remain, and registrations are rejected once capacity is reached. Events and registrations are persisted in DynamoDB, and each successful registration is published to an SQS queue for downstream processing (e.g. confirmation emails, analytics).

endpoints.purpose: Create a new event with title, date and capacity; returns the generated event id.
List all events with their capacity and current registration count.
Retrieve a single event including remaining capacity; 404 if not found.

Register an attendee (name, email) for the event; stores the registration in DynamoDB and publishes a message to SQS. Returns 409 if the event is full, 404 if the event does not exist, 409 if the attendee is already registered.
List registrations for a given event.
Liveness/readiness check reporting service and dependency status.

aws_resources.name: events
aws_resources.justification: Stores event records (title, date, capacity, registered_count). Atomic conditional UpdateItem on registered_count enforces the capacity limit; read by the event list/detail endpoints.

aws_resources.name: registrations
aws_resources.justification: Stores each attendee registration keyed by event_id (partition) and registration_id (sort) so registrations for an event can be queried directly; also backs duplicate-email checks via a GSI.

aws_resources.name: registration-events
aws_resources.justification: The spec requires every successful registration to be published to a queue for downstream processing; the application calls SendMessage after a registration is committed.

aws_resources.name: registration-events-dlq
aws_resources.justification: Redrive target for registration-events so registration messages that repeatedly fail downstream processing are retained rather than lost.

aws_resources.name: event-registration-service-role
aws_resources.justification: Least-privilege policy granting the backend service GetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem/Query/Scan on the two DynamoDB tables and SendMessage on the registration queue.

aws_resources.name: /cloudforge/event-registration-service
aws_resources.justification: Log group for application logs and a metric/alarm on queue depth and rejected-registration counts for operational visibility.

assumptions: No authentication or authorisation is specified; all endpoints are open and an 'organiser' is simply any caller of POST /events.
Event ids and registration ids are server-generated UUID4 strings.
Event date is accepted and stored as an ISO-8601 date string; no timezone handling or past-date validation beyond format checking.
Capacity is enforced with a DynamoDB conditional atomic increment (registered_count < capacity) so concurrent registrations cannot oversell; a failed condition returns HTTP 409.
A full event returns 409 Conflict with an explanatory error body rather than 400.
An attendee email may only register once per event; duplicates return 409.
The SQS message is sent after the registration item is written; a send failure is logged and returns 202-style success detail rather than rolling back, since the registration itself succeeded.
No downstream consumer is part of this specification, so no Lambda or API Gateway is planned — the backend runs as its own service and calls DynamoDB and SQS directly.
No secrets are required; AWS credentials and endpoint URLs come from environment variables (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL for LocalStack), so Secrets Manager is not planned.
Standard (non-FIFO) SQS queue is sufficient as ordering is not required.
Pagination is not specified; list endpoints return up to a bounded page size (default 100) with an optional cursor.
